p: Here's a secret: plenty of grown-ups enjoy these places just as much as the kids. If you're planning to join in, wear something you can actually move in, have a quick stretch first, and pace yourself, because bouncing is a lot more tiring than it looks. Ten minutes in, you'll understand why children sleep so well afterwards.

For the youngsters, the usual rules apply: no zips, buckles or jewellery, long hair tied back and a quick chat about taking turns and minding smaller children. Arrive a bit early to sort shoes and coats, and if it's a party, give guests a clear arrival time so nobody misses half the session.

Bristol's family attractions are brilliant for rounding off the day. We The Curious, the hands-on science centre on Millennium Square, is ideal for inquisitive kids, while the Bristol Zoo Project, on the edge of the city, gives animals and visitors loads of space. Ashton Court Estate offers huge grounds, deer park and woodland walks with views back over the city, and is home to the famous balloon fiesta every summer. Up on Brandon Hill, Cabot Tower gives a free climb to some of the best views over Bristol. And if you need a treat on the way home, the city's independent cafés and bakeries in areas like Gloucester Road won't let you down. Bristol really does have something for every mood.
